plain.text: Herod the ruler heard about Jesus and thought John the Baptist had risen from the dead. Matthew explains that Herod had imprisoned John for condemning his marriage to his brother's wife, Herodias. At Herod's birthday, Herodias' daughter danced, and Herod promised her anything. Prompted by her mother, she asked for John's head on a platter, and Herod had John beheaded. John's disciples buried him and told Jesus.

Jesus withdrew by boat to a quiet place, but crowds followed. He had compassion and healed their sick. In the evening the disciples wanted to send people away to buy food. Jesus said, You give them something to eat. They had only five loaves and two fish. Jesus looked up to heaven, gave thanks, broke the loaves, and the disciples handed them out. Everyone ate and was satisfied, about five thousand men besides women and children, and twelve baskets of leftovers were collected.

Jesus sent the disciples ahead by boat and went up a mountain to pray. In the night, the boat was battered by waves. Jesus came to them walking on the water, and they cried out in fear. He said, Take courage! It is I. Don't be afraid. Peter asked to come to him, and walked on the water, but when he saw the wind he was afraid and began to sink. Lord, save me! Jesus caught him: why did you doubt? When they climbed into the boat, the wind stopped, and the disciples worshipped him as the Son of God.
At Gennesaret people brought all their sick to Jesus and begged to touch the edge of his cloak, and all who touched it were healed.

summary.bigIdea: After John's death, Jesus feeds a huge crowd and walks on water, showing he can be trusted in need and in fear.
points: Herod has John the Baptist killed.
Jesus feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fish.
Peter walks on water, sinks, and Jesus catches him.
summary.reflection: Peter began to sink when he looked at the wind. What helps you keep your eyes on Jesus?
